newsitem.title: UK: London gold fluctuates after U.S. inflation data.
newsitem.headline: London gold fluctuates after U.S. inflation data.

text.p: Precious metals prices fluctuated around earlier intraday highs on Wednesday afternoon after the latest batch of U.S. economic data wiped away any latent inflation fears.
U.S. July retail sales rose 0.6 percent, largely matching expectations, while the U.S. July PPI fell 0.1 pct, the seventh consecutive monthly decline.
Wall Street rallied with the Dow up 50 points in the first few minutes following lower-than-expected retail sales figures and the seventh straight month of falling producer prices.
The long bond was up 1-2/32, pushing the yield down to 6.59 percent as the figures eased any fears of an interest rate hikes, analysts said.

Gold fixed down $2.40 from the morning level at $326.20 per ounce and wiped out losses after the fixing as New York's Comex December futures contract recoupling an early set back to be $2.00 firmer at $332.80.
However the mood of the market remained largely negative with dealers forecasting gold remaining in a $325-$330 range, at least for this week.

As if to confirm that sentiment, one month implied gold lease rates were marked up sharply to 2.29 percent from 1.93 percent on Tuesday suggesting funds and producers may be borrowing again to fund short positions and hedges.
"There is not much to go for but upside resistance might be eroding slightly," one dealer said.
Silver also wobbled with gold but by 1430 GMT was pushing against the $4.50 resistance which had stopped it a week ago.
Dealers said silver had attracted little notice since an attempt to fill a gap on the price charts between $4.50-$4.55 had aborted at the beginning of last week.
However the platinum group metals were less willing followers of gold after both had opened positively and failed to hold gains posted in Asia.
Platinum was indicated at $437.00/$440.00 up $2.50 but of its early peak and palladium was down $2.00 at $244.50/$227.50.
Dealers said lease rates for the metals were lower with tightness easing from the squeeze levels of two months ago before Russia began its belated 1997 export campaign.
Platinum was quoted at about 12-15 percent and palladium was available at 40-60 percent for a month.
